saints.name: St. John Baptist de Rossi
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A Roman priest who gave himself wholly to the poor, the sick, and the outcasts of the city…
biography: Giovanni Battista de' Rossi was born on 22 February 1698 at Voltaggio, in the Genoese territory, the last of four children of poor but pious parents. Brought to Rome in 1711, he studied under the Jesuits of the Collegium Romanum and the Dominicans of the Minerva. Epilepsy, which first struck him then, dogged him all his life, and he was ordained on 8 March 1721 only by special dispensation.

He gave himself to the neglected of Rome: he founded a hospice for homeless women near San Galla, and sought out prisoners, the sick, and the carters and herdsmen who came in from the Campagna. Canon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin from 1737, he sold his cousin's fine house and gave the money to the poor.

Long afraid to hear confessions lest a seizure interrupt them, he became one of the most sought-after confessors in Rome, called a second Philip Neri, and Clement XII freed him from choir duties for the confessional's sake. Worn out by labour and by strokes, he died on 23 May 1764. He was beatified by Pius IX in 1860 and canonized by Leo XIII on 8 December 1881.
saints.knownFor: His tireless ministry to Rome's poor and in the confessional.
